intro: Meghalaya's limestone hills and heavy rainfall have created some of India's most unusual landscapes: deep river gorges, waterfalls pouring off plateaus, bridges grown from the roots of rubber fig trees, and cave systems that run for kilometres underground. Sohra (Cherrapunji) and Mawsynram, on the southern edge of the Khasi Hills, are among the wettest places on Earth.

The best adventure in Meghalaya is on foot, underground and on its rivers. This guide covers the main activities and when to go. For Shillong, food, markets and sightseeing, see our Meghalaya travel guide.
quickAnswer: The best adventure activities in Meghalaya are the trek down to the double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat, the David Scott Trail, caving at Mawmluh near Sohra and in the Jaintia and Garo hills, kayaking, snorkelling and camping on the clear Umngot river at Dawki and Shnongpdeng, ziplining at Mawkdok and canyon walks at Laitlum. October to April is best; the monsoon brings very heavy rain.
takeaways: The Nongriat trek involves thousands of steps down (and back up) to the double-decker root bridge.
Meghalaya has many of India's longest caves; go only with experienced local guides.
The Umngot is clearest from about November to April, the season for kayaking and snorkelling at Shnongpdeng.
Ziplines at Mawkdok Dympep valley between Shillong and Sohra are among the longest in the North East.
The monsoon brings very heavy rain, slippery trails and swollen rivers; plan most activities for October to April.

items.name: Nongriat and the double-decker root bridge
body: From Tyrna village near Sohra, a trail of about 3,000 steps descends through forest and over single root bridges and steel suspension bridges to Nongriat, where two living root bridges stand one above the other. Stay overnight in a guesthouse or return the same day; the climb back is steep. Natural pools beyond the village are good for a swim in the dry season.

items.name: David Scott Trail
body: A historic trail of about 16 km from near Mawphlang towards Lad Mawphlang, following an old route through the Khasi Hills, with river crossings and valley views.

items.name: Laitlum Canyons
body: A viewpoint on the edge of the plateau near Shillong, with steep steps down into the valley for those who want to walk.

sections.heading: Caving
paras: Meghalaya has many of India's longest and deepest known caves, mapped over decades by local and international caving expeditions. Krem Liat Prah in the Jaintia Hills is among the longest natural caves in India.

items.name: Mawmluh Cave, near Sohra
body: A long cave with river passages, near the Sohra market, explored with local guides. Waterproof shoes and a headlamp are essential.

items.name: Siju Cave, Garo Hills
body: A river cave near the Simsang river in the Garo Hills, next to the Balpakram region, with bats and limestone formations.

items.name: Show caves
body: Mawsmai cave near Sohra is lit and has a walkway, a good introduction for families.

items.name: Umngot river at Dawki and Shnongpdeng
body: The Umngot is famous for water so clear that boats appear to float in the dry season. Riverside camps at Shnongpdeng offer kayaking, snorkelling and cliff jumping.

items.name: Umiam Lake
body: A large reservoir near Shillong with a water-sports complex for kayaking and boating.

items.name: Waterfalls
body: Nohkalikai, Seven Sisters and Wei Sawdong are spectacular, especially in and after the monsoon. Viewing points are safe; climbing down to pools can be dangerous in high water.

items.name: Mawkdok Dympep valley
body: Ziplines cross the valley between Shillong and Sohra, some among the longest in the North East, with views over the gorge.

sections.heading: Getting there and a sample trip
paras: Guwahati airport and railway station in Assam are the main gateways, about three hours by road from Shillong. Shillong is the base for Laitlum, Mawphlang, Umiam and Mawkdok; Sohra or Tyrna for Nongriat and the caves; and Dawki or Shnongpdeng for the Umngot.
Roads between these bases are good but slow, and many adventure sites are run by village communities that charge small fees and provide guides. Carry cash.

Nongriat trek from Tyrna, overnight in the village
Climb back up, drive to Shnongpdeng for kayaking and camping

safety: Go caving only with experienced local guides, and never enter caves in heavy rain when they can flood.
Wear shoes with good grip; root bridges and steps are slippery.
Do not swim or cliff-jump when the Umngot is high or murky.
Keep to viewpoints at waterfalls, especially in the monsoon.
Respect village rules and fees; many sites are community-managed.
packing: Waterproof shoes or sandals with grip
A rain jacket, even in the dry season
Quick-dry clothes and a change of clothes
Cash for village fees and guides

faqs.q: What are the best adventure activities in Meghalaya?
faqs.a: The Nongriat root bridge trek, caving at Mawmluh and Siju, kayaking and snorkelling on the Umngot, ziplining at Mawkdok and walks at Laitlum.

faqs.q: How difficult is the Nongriat trek?
faqs.a: It involves about 3,000 steep steps down and back up. Most reasonably fit people manage it in a day, or stay overnight at Nongriat.

faqs.q: When is the Umngot river clear?

faqs.a: With experienced local guides, proper lights and outside the rains, yes. Do not enter caves alone or in heavy rain.
